whatItIs.text: Leaf cabbage — a brassica grown for loose leaves that never form a head, in curly, Tuscan (cavolo nero), and Russian types.

historyNote.text: Kale was cultivated in the eastern Mediterranean and Anatolia by 2000 BC at the latest; curly and flat types grew in 4th-century-BC Greece, and the Romans knew their ancestors as Sabellian kale. It survives to −15 °C and turns sweeter after frost.

howToChoose.text: Choose deep-coloured, springy leaves without yellowing or limpness; smaller leaves are milder and the stems of Tuscan types need less stripping.

storage.text: Refrigerate loosely bagged in the crisper, unwashed until use. The rulebook has the window.
storage.note: leafy-green windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Rubbed with oil and salt, even tired kale crisps into chips; it melts into white-bean soup, braises, and the Portuguese soup caldo verde.

substitutions.note: much tenderer; add at the end, halve the cook time
direct swaps; Tuscan is sweeter and softer
